title: RFP-ready checklist + negotiation notes for Dedicated Inference
content:
Purpose:
Quick, tactical doc for AE/SEs & procurement-facing AMs to take into an RFP/negotiation with platform or infra teams. Goal = shorten cycles by being procurement-ready: pre-bake language, metrics, fallback options and commercial levers so legal + procurement can sign without long back-and-forths.

TL;DR messaging (one-liners to use early):
- Predictable throughput at scale — dedicated GPU pools with committed throughput guarantees you can reason about in capacity planning.
- Isolation you can audit — compute and tenant isolation options (VPC, hardware affinity) to reduce noisy-neighbor and data surface risk.
- SLAs that map to business outcomes — latency and availability SLAs aligned to route-level SLOs and clear remedies.
- Procurement-ready tradeoffs — configurable bandwidth between cost and headroom (burst pools, reserved slots, failover tiers).

Primary buyer personas and cues: 
- Platform/Infra Lead (primary technical buyer): cares about isolation, predictable tail latency, capacity planning, and failover. Questions about scheduling, affinity, and observability.
- SRE/Performance Engineer: asks about p95/p99 numbers, throttling behavior, KV cache warmup, cold-start characteristics, and SLO mapping.
- Procurement/Legal: wants caps on liability, clear remedies, uptime credits, and simple exit terms.
- Product/ML engineering: wants predictable per-request latency and deterministic behavior under load for user-facing features.

Negotiation playbook (practical steps + scripts):
1) Discovery (first call): ask for target qps, typical input length distribution, burst patterns, data residency constraints, and failure tolerance. Record sample prompt sizes.
2) Anchor on value, not just price: translate throughput to UX metrics (requests/sec -> transactions/hour -> user 95th percentile latency).
3) Offer modular guarantees: baseline reserved throughput (committed RPS) + burst allowance (best-effort or metered). This lets buyers pick cost vs headroom.
4) Push for objective SLAs: use measurable metrics (p95 latency, p99 latency, sustained throughput per-minute) rather than vague language.
5) Scope of isolation: define "isolation" options explicitly: tenant-affine NVLink locality, dedicated nodes, single-tenant pools, and VPC/private control plane.
6) Remedies and credits: prefer service credits tied to downtime windows or sustained SLA misses. Avoid heavy fixed-penalty liabilities.

Suggested negotiation script snippets:
- For procurement: "We can commit to a baseline throughput of X requests/minute at p95 <= Y ms with a dedicated pool. If that baseline is exceeded we provide a defined burst buffer and automated scaling paths; we also expose telemetry for your engineers to verify usage."
- For legal on liability: "We cap consequential damages per the contract value of the annual commitment and provide service credit remedies for SLA breaches. For sensitive workloads we offer private deployment options with additional compliance controls."

SLA primitives to propose (concrete wording examples for legal):
- Availability: "Service Availability shall be no less than 99.95% per billing month for dedicated capacity endpoints specified in Appendix A."
- Latency: "For the model endpoints listed in Appendix A, the Provider shall maintain p95 token generation latency <= 120ms and p99 <= 450ms measured over rolling 24h windows under the committed throughput profile."
- Throughput guarantee: "Committed Throughput: Provider guarantees sustained throughput of N tokens/sec (or M requests/min) across the reserved pool, with documented policies for burst handling and rate-limiting during contention."
- Isolation: "Isolation Guarantee: The Provider shall not co-locate unassociated tenants on dedicated pool nodes and will maintain compute affinity such that noisy-neighbor interference is mitigated. Customer may elect single-tenant pool for an additional fee."
- Remedies: "Customer is eligible for service credits equal to X% of monthly fees pro-rated by outage duration for SLA breaches beyond the remediation window. Service credits are sole and exclusive remedy."

Common redlines and recommended concessions (deal-velocity minded):
- Redline: Unlimited liability / heavy indemnity. Concede: standard liability cap tied to committed spend, carve-outs for gross negligence.
- Redline: Absolute throughput/latency guarantees irrespective of customer input distribution. Concede: guarantees tied to committed workload profile and documented input distributions; re-baseline if customer behavior deviates > 25%.
- Redline: On-premise-installation acceptance tests that require infra changes. Concede: provide a defined acceptance plan with test harness + runbook; limit timeboxed remediation and re-tests.

Competitive notes (quick takeaways vs. common vendor archetypes):
- Generic cloud vendor: ± strong ops and global footprint, weaker model-level optimizations and cost predictability. Emphasize Redwood wins on per-token economics, model-tuned runtime, and predictable dedicated throughput.
- Self-hosted inference stacks: ± full control but heavy ops burden. Frame Redwood as "managed predictable" — we take on ops and guarantee throughput SLAs.
- Single-model inference providers: ± optimized for single model stacks, but limited model catalog and migration flexibility. Redwood sells multi-model routing + fallback to cheaper variants to keep apps up when primary model capacity constrained.

Technical appendix (for SEs to attach to RFP response):
- Measurement & instrumentation: We will provide token-level telemetry, request traces, and per-pool utilization dashboards; we expose an API for per-route metrics and tracing hooks.
- Cold-start behavior: Quantify cold-start latency (median, p95) and KV cache warmup recommendations (recommended warmup samples per model).
- Batching/caching policy: Default batching window, max batch size, and suggestions to hit throughput/cost tradeoffs with examples (e.g., for 20 req/s with average 256 tokens, recommended pool = 4 x A40-equivalent nodes).
- Compatibility matrix: supported model formats, quantization profiles, and fallback strategy mapping.
- Disaster recovery: cross-region failover approach, RTO targets for private vs hosted, and runbook for manual failover.

Procurement FAQ (short answers to speed up threads):
- Q: How do you measure sustained throughput?
  A: Throughput is measured as committed tokens/sec averaged over 5-minute windows across the reserved pool; sustained breach triggers scaling or credit events per contract.
- Q: How do you prevent noisy neighbors?
  A: Dedicated pools are isolated at the node level; we provide affinity placement and soft reservation to ensure latency isolation.
- Q: Can we audit isolation?
  A: Yes — we can provide placement reports, telemetry exports, and for Private deployments offer on-prem or VPC-based inspection options.
- Q: What happens on bursts?
  A: Contract defines burst buffer: either metered overage, best-effort burst from shared spare capacity, or automatic spillage to lower-cost model variants depending on customer selection.

Objections and rebuttals (AE/SE cheat-sheet):
- Objection: "We need absolute p99 at 50ms."
  Rebuttal: "We can design a dedicated pool and an operational plan to target that for narrow prompt distributions — let’s capture your prompt size histogram and target traffic window, then we can propose a calibrated commit."
- Objection: "Why not self-host?"
  Rebuttal: "Self-hosting shifts full lifecycle ops and costs to your team; with Redwood you get tuned runtime kernels, model routing, and an SLA-backed operational commitment so your team can focus on product features."

Commercial levers to accelerate close: 
- Short-term pilot credits + 3-month committed conversion price guarantee.
- Bundled observability (extended telemetry retention) as a purchase add-on to reduce procurement friction.
- Tiered exit: allow short notice exit during pilot window but transition to standard termination notice on annual commits.

Next steps / action items (owner tags):
- SE: build sample throughput calc for target account (jira:GTMP-7821) — DUE 2025-09-18 (Marco Ruiz)
- AE: capture prompt size histogram + peak windows from prospect — DUE 2025-09-14 (Sofia Nguyen)
- Legal: prepare Appendix A SLA template with placeholders for committed throughput and endpoint list — DUE 2025-09-22 (Priya Menon)
- GtM ops: prepare pricing delta table for burst options and private pool premiums — DUE 2025-09-20 (Daniel Park)

Quick WIP notes (raw, keep informal):
- TODO: add per-GPU throughput examples (A100, H100 equivalents) + cost per 1M tokens calc.
- TODO: gather customer redlines from last 6 closed deals and synthesize top-5.
- Link to internal: confluence/gtm/dedicated-playbook and repo/inference/benchmarks (add actual links in final).

Bottom line for sellers: Bring a measured, configurable commitment to procurement — pair a concrete throughput/latency promise (tied to a documented workload profile) with optional isolation modes and clearly scoped remedies. That combo is what accelerates procurement decisions for mid-enterprise and larger accounts.
